newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAKIA REVISES UPWARD 1996 SUGAR BEET CROP FORECAST.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAKIA REVISES UPWARD 1996 SUGAR BEET CROP FORECAST.

text.p: The Slovak Statistical Bureau (SUSR) on Tuesday said it had revised slightly upwards its 1996 sugar beet crop to 1.60-1.65 million tonnes, from a previous estimate of 1.57-1.64 million tonnes.
"Sufficient rainfall favourably influenced the sugar beet crop, which is expected to be 38.1 percent higher than last year," SUSR said in a statement.
But, it warned: "Ongoing rain unfavourably affects the sugar content and the volume of harvest losses".
The bureau said the yield per hectare of the 1996 crop should rise to 38.14 tonnes according to the latest test as of September 15, from 37.63 tonnes forecasted to August 15.

Sown area rose by 22.1 percent to 42,600 hectares in 1996 from 34,900 hectares in 1995, the bureau said, adding that 34,335 hectares were actually harvested last year. It did not give an estimate of expected harvested area for 1996.
No percentage sugar content per beet forecast was immediately available.
Slovakia's 1995 sugar beet crop was 1.176 million tonnes, with the yield per hectare of 34.26 tonnes.
